opportunities.title: Explain how AI changes the shape of work, not only the number of jobs
opportunities.readerValue: Readers can distinguish tasks, jobs and organizations, then see where judgment, responsibility and decision rights move when agents take on more work.
opportunities.facts: AIDB published an August 23 Long Reads edition synthesizing the first 25 essays in Every's Thesis Statements collection; the collection and four exact primary essays were accessible.
opportunities.attributedInterpretation: AIDB argues that the job-loss question is too blunt: automation of stable tasks may increase framing and verification work, AI may expand possible work, organizations may become human-agent systems, and value may shift toward judgment, discernment, connection, taste and responsibility.
opportunities.laidiesInference: This earns a new Big Picture watch theme, not an article yet. LAiDIES should explain the task-to-system-to-decision chain and include unpaid work, worker power and distributional consequences; empirical outcomes and non-frontier perspectives are still missing.

opportunities.title: Teach agentic delegation through permissions, boundaries and review
opportunities.readerValue: Readers can understand why giving AI tools changes the job from writing a better prompt to defining access, approval, review and the consequences of a mistake.
opportunities.facts: Mollick published a July 23 guide that distinguishes low-stakes chat from agentic work and illustrates cloud-hosted and local-computer workflows.
opportunities.attributedInterpretation: Mollick recommends learning by delegating a real task, treating agent work more like management than chat, keeping approvals on for consequential actions and limiting what an agent can touch.
opportunities.laidiesInference: The durable mechanism is valuable, but product rankings, plan prices, mode names and capability comparisons must be rebuilt from current official evidence. The useful lesson is permissions plus evaluation, not a universal product recommendation.
